title: Turn up the harm

predict.q: The external cost per unit rises from 0 to 8. What happens?

options.s: The market quantity falls, because buyers now face higher costs.
options.fb: Buyers do not pay the external cost, so MPB and Q1 do not move. Only MSB moves.

options.s: The market quantity stays the same, the optimum falls and the welfare loss grows.
options.fb: Q1 stays at 100; Q* falls from 100 to 60; the welfare loss grows from 0 to 160.

options.s: The market quantity and the optimum fall together, so there is no welfare loss.
options.fb: Q1 is set by MPB and MPC, which ignore the harm; only Q* moves, so a gap opens.

options.s: The optimum rises, because society now gets more from each unit.
options.fb: An external cost lowers MSB, so the optimum falls.

task: Move the external cost slider and watch MSB, Q* and the shaded triangle.

target.do: Move the slider from 0 to 8, then press Check.

takeaway: The market ignores external costs, so a bigger external cost means a bigger gap between Q1 and Q*.
